draft.title: Reform and reaction
card: Pyotr Stolypin was prime minister from 1906 to 1911. He wanted to calm unrest by strengthening the empire, using both reform and force.
Stolypin's land reforms let peasants leave the village commune and farm their own plots. He hoped a class of prosperous, loyal farmers would support the tsar.

Special military courts dealt quickly with people accused of revolt, and many were hanged. The hangman's rope became known as 'Stolypin's necktie'. The government also policed the press and political groups.
The reforms helped some peasants, but most stayed poor and land hunger remained. Stolypin was shot dead in 1911, and by 1914 strikes were growing again.
draft.remember: Stolypin tried to win loyalty with land reform and to crush protest with force, and neither settled the empire.

a.q: What was the main aim of Stolypin's land reforms?
opts: To create loyal, well-off peasant farmers who backed the tsar
To hand all noble estates over to the village communes
To move peasants into factories in the growing cities
To give peasants a say in the running of the Duma
a.why: Stolypin hoped that peasants who owned their own farms would care about order and support the tsar. The reforms let peasants leave the commune, so they did not strengthen it. They were about land, not about political power in the Duma.
a.clue: Think about who Stolypin hoped would become loyal to the tsar.

b.q: By 1914, why had Stolypin's mix of reform and repression failed to settle the empire?
opts: Most peasants stayed poor and strikes were rising again
Stolypin's courts were ended and unrest quickly faded
The reforms gave peasants plenty of land, yet they wanted more
The Duma was closed and then ruled without any limits
b.why: The land reforms helped only some peasants, and repression did not remove the causes of anger. Strikes grew again by 1914, so the empire was still unsettled. The courts did not stop unrest, and the reforms did not leave peasants with plenty of land.
b.clue: Ask whether the causes of anger had actually gone away.
